blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 1.1
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 1.1

blocks.text: BOOK I — ŚĀMBHAVOPĀYA
blocks.directed: [long pause] BOOK I — ŚĀMBHAVOPĀYA

blocks.text: चैतन्यमात्मा
blocks.directed: [slowly] चैतन्यमात्मा

blocks.text: Caitanyam ātmā.
blocks.directed: Caitanyam ātmā.

blocks.text: Consciousness is the Self.
blocks.directed: Consciousness is the Self.

blocks.text: The Biggest Plot Twist in Human History.
blocks.directed: The Biggest Plot Twist in Human History.

blocks.text: Ladies and gentlemen.
blocks.directed: Ladies and gentlemen.

blocks.text: Vasugupta has entered the building.
blocks.directed: Vasugupta has entered the building.

blocks.text: And he has decided to open with a statement so outrageous that the rest of Indian philosophy is going to need a cigarette.
blocks.directed: And he has decided to open with a statement so outrageous that the rest of Indian philosophy is going to need a cigarette.

blocks.text: You are consciousness.
blocks.directed: You are consciousness.

blocks.text: Not you possess consciousness.
blocks.directed: Not you possess consciousness.

blocks.text: Not your brain produces a lovely little subjective experience and that’s what you fundamentally are.
blocks.directed: Not your brain produces a lovely little subjective experience and that’s what you fundamentally are.

blocks.text: No.
blocks.directed: No.

blocks.text: The thing that you actually are — ātman — is caitanya.
blocks.directed: The thing that you actually are — ātman — is caitanya.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack this carefully.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack this carefully.

blocks.text: Caitanya comes from the Sanskrit family of cit, awareness or consciousness. But Kṣemarāja is not talking about ordinary, fluctuating mental awareness.
blocks.directed: Caitanya comes from the Sanskrit family of cit, awareness or consciousness. But Kṣemarāja is not talking about ordinary, fluctuating mental awareness.

blocks.text: He’s talking about consciousness as fundamentally free, self-revealing, and endowed with unlimited powers of knowing and acting.
blocks.directed: He’s talking about consciousness as fundamentally free, self-revealing, and endowed with unlimited powers of knowing and acting.

blocks.text: That last part is crucial.
blocks.directed: That last part is crucial.

blocks.text: In Trika, Śiva is not merely a cosmic spectator.
blocks.directed: In Trika, Śiva is not merely a cosmic spectator.

blocks.text: He’s not sitting in some metaphysical armchair thinking, “Lovely universe, shame I can’t do anything about it.”
blocks.directed: He’s not sitting in some metaphysical armchair thinking, “Lovely universe, shame I can’t do anything about it.”

blocks.text: He’s prakāśa, the luminous manifestation of reality, inseparable from vimarśa, its reflexive awareness of itself.
blocks.directed: He’s prakāśa, the luminous manifestation of reality, inseparable from vimarśa, its reflexive awareness of itself.

blocks.text: And that self-awareness is inseparable from svātantrya — absolute freedom.
blocks.directed: And that self-awareness is inseparable from svātantrya — absolute freedom.

blocks.text: So what does Vasugupta actually mean?
blocks.directed: So what does Vasugupta actually mean?

blocks.text: Your deepest nature is not a little individual observer trapped inside a body looking out at a separate universe.
blocks.directed: Your deepest nature is not a little individual observer trapped inside a body looking out at a separate universe.

blocks.text: Your deepest nature is the very conscious reality through which that entire distinction between observer and observed becomes manifest.
blocks.directed: Your deepest nature is the very conscious reality through which that entire distinction between observer and observed becomes manifest.

blocks.text: The universe isn’t an alien object standing opposite Śiva.
blocks.directed: The universe isn’t an alien object standing opposite Śiva.

blocks.text: It’s Śiva expressing his own nature.
blocks.directed: It’s Śiva expressing his own nature.

blocks.text: And you, apparently, have spent your entire life under the impression that you’re just some bloke with a calendar and a digestive system.
blocks.directed: And you, apparently, have spent your entire life under the impression that you’re just some bloke with a calendar and a digestive system.

blocks.text: An extraordinary administrative error.
blocks.directed: An extraordinary administrative error.

blocks.text: The philosophical point: In Trika metaphysics, individual consciousness is not ultimately separate from universal consciousness. Recognition, pratyabhijñā, means realising an identity that was never actually absent.
blocks.directed: The philosophical point: In Trika metaphysics, individual consciousness is not ultimately separate from universal consciousness. Recognition, pratyabhijñā, means realising an identity that was never actually absent.

blocks.text: And that’s sūtra one.
blocks.directed: And that’s sūtra one.

blocks.text: He’s barely started.
blocks.directed: He’s barely started.
